Application Areas: Development of therapeutic strategies against Clostridioides difficile infection and antibiotic resistance
Elucidation of regulatory networks in anaerobic pathogens for infectious disease control
Optimization of anaerobic biodegradation and syntrophic metabolism for biofuel production and wastewater treatment
Understanding fundamental mechanisms of archaeal and bacterial transcription machinery
Characterization of iron-sulfur cluster functions in anaerobic bioenergetics
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Structure-Function Correlation in Transcriptional Regulation: Integrating high-resolution X-ray crystallography with in vitro DNA binding assays to define the mechanistic basis of gene regulation (e.g., Determining the 1.9 Å crystal structure of cdPadR1 and using EMSA to identify specific inverted repeat motifs for auto-regulation in C. difficile).

Biochemical Dissection of Protein Assembly and Stability: Employing genetic knockout strategies combined with biophysical characterization to isolate the specific roles of structural domains in complex macromolecular assembly (e.g., Using site-directed mutagenesis and Fe-S cluster reconstitution to demonstrate that ferredoxin-like domains in Methanosarcina acetivorans Rpo3 are critical for RNA polymerase subunit assembly rather than initial dimer formation).

Multi-Omics Integration for Metabolic Pathway Elucidation: Combining shotgun proteomics, stable isotope metabolomics, and enzymatic kinetic analysis to map complex metabolic networks in syntrophic organisms (e.g., Utilizing 13C-labeling and 2D-PAGE in Syntrophus aciditrophicus to identify pyrophosphate-producing ligases and protein conduits for reverse electron transfer in aromatic acid degradation).

Phosphorylation-Dependent Regulatory Mechanism Analysis: Investigating the dynamic structural changes of response regulators to understand signal transduction in challenging anaerobic pathogens (e.g., Demonstrating that RR_1586 in C. difficile undergoes phosphorylation-dependent dimer-to-tetramer oligomerization, which modulates its DNA binding affinity and regulon specificity via bacterial one-hybrid assays).
Summary Description: Elizabeth Karr is a structural biologist and molecular microbiologist specializing in the regulatory mechanisms of anaerobic pathogens and syntrophic bacteria. Her research focuses on Clostridioides difficile and methanogenic archaea, utilizing X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and multi-omics approaches to elucidate gene regulation and metabolic pathways. Key contributions include determining the structural basis of transcriptional auto-regulation in C. difficile and defining the role of iron-sulfur clusters in archaeal RNA polymerase assembly. Additionally, she has characterized enzymatic mechanisms in syntrophic partners like Syntrophus aciditrophicus, revealing novel strategies for energy conservation in anaerobic biodegradation. Her work bridges fundamental structural biology with translational goals in infectious disease control and bioenergy production, providing critical insights into the physiology of organisms that thrive in oxygen-depleted environments.
